state.misconception_label: Does not know units of area should be squared

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: James has answered a question on the area of a trapezium and got an answer of \( 54 \). Behind the star he has written the units that he used. \( 54 \, \bigstar \) Which of the following units could be correct? I got \( m \) because I added the side lengths instead of multiplying.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you explain why you think adding the side lengths instead of multiplying would give you the correct units for area in this case?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, I'm not really sure now that you've asked me that... I think I was just confused because we add things together sometimes in maths? But like, when we do area we multiply the length and width, so wouldn't the units multiply too? Is that why it should be m squared instead of just m?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you think of a time when we convert units, like when we go from kilometers to meters? How do we handle squared units in that situation?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, so like when we convert from kilometers to meters we multiply by 1000, right? But I'm still a bit confused about how that works with squared units... does that mean if we have square kilometers we'd have to multiply by like 1000 squared or something? That seems really big.
